name: Skyworks Solutions, Inc.

profile.description: Skyworks Solutions, founded in 1962 and headquartered in Irvine, California, designs and manufactures analog and mixed-signal semiconductors - RF front-end modules, power amplifiers, filters, timing devices, power isolators, and wireless SoCs - for smartphones, automotive, broadband, data center, industrial, and defense markets. FY2025 (ended October 3, 2025) revenue was $4.09B. CEO Philip Brace succeeded Liam Griffin in February 2025. Fiscal 2026 quarterly revenue ran $1.035B (Q1), $944M (Q2), and $935M (Q3, -3% YoY). Skyworks is merging with Qorvo (Qorvo holders receive $32.50 cash plus 0.960 SWKS shares per share); both companies' shareholders have approved the deal, which remains subject to regulatory approvals.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Revenue peaked at $5.49B in FY2022 and has fallen to $4.09B in FY2025 as mobile content at its largest customer came under pressure; diversification into automotive, broadband/Wi-Fi, data center timing, and power isolation (from the 2021 Silicon Labs I&A acquisition) is real but has not offset the mobile decline [4]. AI Deployment (1/2): Management positions Skyworks' timing, power, and connectivity products for AI-driven edge devices and data centers, but no quantified AI revenue or internal AI savings are disclosed [5][6]. Market Share (1/2): Skyworks is one of a handful of scaled RF front-end suppliers, but share at its largest mobile customer is eroding and the Qorvo merger is partly a defensive response to scale pressure [1][5]. Pipeline (1/2): The Qorvo combination and next-generation Wi-Fi 7 and 5G Advanced platforms are named, but without specific product launch timelines or revenue visibility [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D of $785.5M equals 19.2% of FY2025 revenue (FMP), up from 15.1% in FY2024, in the upper range for analog/RF peers [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Skyworks' purpose of 'connecting everyone and everything, all the time' is clear and connects its RF work to global connectivity, but it is not distinctive versus RF peers [5]. Community Impact (0/2): Skyworks publishes sustainability reports and Sustainalytics rates its controversy level at 1 of 5, but no distinctive, dollar-quantified community program was found; shareholders rejected a 2025 proposal (21.9% support) seeking fuller Scope 3 emissions disclosure [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor shows 3.6/5 with 62% recommending to a friend, and no tenure or turnover data was found [6]. Insider Buying (1/2): FMP shows no open-market purchases or sales in the last three quarters, with activity dominated by equity grants - a neutral signal [8].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored (dividend sleeve, 12 weight units, weighted sum 8.86). D/E of 11.9% scores 1.0 and forward P/E of 15.1 scores 1.0 [3]. ROE of 5.1% scores 0.34, revenue growth of -3.1% YoY scores 0.56, and the 7.2% profit margin scores 0.36 [3]. The 5yr revenue CAGR of 4.0% (FY2020 $3.36B to FY2025 $4.09B, derived from FMP statements) scores 0.60 [4]. Dividend metrics carry the score: 12 consecutive years paid (2x weight) and 11 consecutive years of increases (through the August 2025 raise to $0.71) both score 1.0, and the 5yr dividend CAGR of 7.3% ($0.50 quarterly in 2021 to $0.71 in 2026, derived from FMP dividend history) scores 1.0 at 2x weight [9]. The 146.7% TTM payout ratio (FMP, GAAP) scores 0 [4]. Daily dollar volume of about $560M clears the liquidity floor.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Skyworks sells physical RF, analog, and power semiconductors; AI cannot substitute for the hardware, and AI-capable smartphones, edge devices, and data centers all require RF front ends, timing, and power isolation [5]. The risk is indirect: AI-driven handset upgrade cycles accrue mainly to processor and memory vendors, while customer insourcing of RF and modem silicon is the more pressing threat to Skyworks' mobile content. AI Opportunity (0/1): Management cites AI as a demand driver for its broad-markets portfolio, but no quantified AI revenue is disclosed, so the tiebreaker point is not awarded [5][6].

infinite_game.summary: Skyworks is responding to a shrinking core - revenue down from $5.49B (FY2022) to $4.09B (FY2025) - with a CEO change in 2025 and a large, scale-driven merger with Qorvo. Through Sinek's lens, these are rational defensive moves, but its purpose statement does not visibly guide strategy, its culture scores are middling, and the merger is framed around scale and synergies rather than a cause.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Connecting everyone and everything, all the time' describes a bigger future, but strategy discussion centers on content gains, customer concentration, and merger synergies rather than the cause [1][5]. It reads more as a tagline than a guiding Just Cause.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Glassdoor shows 3.6/5 with 86% CEO approval and 62% recommending the company, which is roughly average for semiconductors [6]. The 2025 board-led CEO succession was orderly, but merger integration with Qorvo will test organizational trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Combining with Qorvo - its closest RF rival - is framed around scale, synergies, and US-based leadership in RF rather than learning from competitors [1]. No evidence was found of management citing rivals as benchmarks for improvement.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Skyworks has expanded beyond mobile into automotive, broadband, data center timing, and power isolation through the Silicon Labs I&A deal, and is now merging with Qorvo [1][4]. These moves are substantial adjacent expansions, not a fundamental reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management raised R&D from $632M (FY2024) to $786M (FY2025) while revenue declined, and committed to a large cash-and-stock merger to secure long-term scale [1][4]. However, paying a dividend at a 147% GAAP payout ratio suggests near-term shareholder optics remain a priority [4].

investment_thesis: Skyworks pairs a pristine balance sheet (D/E of 11.9%, current ratio of 3.1) with a 3.2% dividend that has grown for 11 straight years, and trades at 15.1x forward earnings [3][4][9]. The pending Qorvo merger, approved by both companies' shareholders, would create a US-based RF and analog leader with greater scale, broader customer reach, and cost synergies at a time when customer insourcing pressures single-vendor RF suppliers [1]. Fiscal 2026 revenue has stabilized around $935M-$1.035B per quarter, and R&D intensity of 19% of revenue keeps the product roadmap funded through the transition [4][5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is a shrinking core and deal risk. Revenue has fallen from $5.49B in FY2022 to $4.09B in FY2025 and is still declining (-3.1% YoY), ROE is 5.1%, and EPS fell 68.6% YoY [3][4]. The 146.7% GAAP payout ratio means the dividend is not covered by earnings, and the August-quarter 2026 dividend and Q3 FY2026 details should be confirmed [4]. The Qorvo merger still requires regulatory approvals, including potential China review, and will add integration risk and dilution; content losses at the largest mobile customer could continue regardless of the deal [1].
key_catalysts: Regulatory clearance and closing of the Qorvo merger, with synergy targets and combined-company guidance
Fiscal Q4 2026 results (fiscal year ended early October) showing whether revenue and margins have bottomed
Broad-markets growth in automotive, Wi-Fi 7, and data center timing offsetting mobile content pressure
key_risks: Regulatory delay or failure of the Qorvo merger, or costly integration and dilution if it closes
Continued content loss at the largest smartphone customer as it insources RF and modem silicon
Dividend coverage: a 146.7% GAAP payout ratio with declining earnings could force the board to freeze or cut the payout
